narrative: OMX30 faces conflicting signals this morning. While the index remains +7.1% above its 200-day MA in established bull trend, technical momentum has clearly deteriorated with MACD rolling over into bearish crossover territory and ADX collapsing to 2.9—indicating weak directional conviction. The global backdrop is unambiguously negative: European bourses led by DAX (-0.99%) are reacting to a sharp bond sell-off, with US 10Y yields spiking 184bps to 4.758% on renewed inflation concerns (Eurozone CPI now 3.3%). RSI at 45.29 is neutral but the Stochastic divergence (K 42.9 vs D 65.0) suggests momentum is fading. Oil's +1.77% rise pressures industrials while yielding cost headwinds hit real estate and tech valuations. Low ADX severity reduces conviction on all tactical calls.
morningBrief: OMX30 opens into a mild headwind with global macro risks elevated. Expect a range-bound to slightly negative session as traders digest the bond sell-off (10Y +184bps) and await 14:30 CET US Jobless Claims—any miss could spike volatility further given VIX already +6.23%. Industrials (28% weight) face dual pressure from rising oil and wider rate-driven discount rates; look for Atlas Copco and Volvo B to underperform. Banks benefit modestly from NIM expansion (SEB, Handelsbanken likely flat-to-positive) but lack conviction given weak ADX. Defensive rotation into AstraZeneca and Essity B may provide some safety bids. Support holds at 3085 (lower Bollinger); resistance at 3180 (50-MA). Key watch: if VIX breaks above 17, expect OMX30 to retest 3120 level intraday. Reduce position sizes ahead of US jobs print.
